plugins.name: Autumn
plugins.description: Golden leaves by day and a red maple at dusk: a warm, cosy Loam in light and in dark.
plugins.author: Michael Hejazi

note.summary: Autumn is a visual theme that dresses Loam in warm paper, copper, and maple tones for light and dark modes, with headings set in Young Serif. It contains only CSS stylesheets, local font files, and preview images, and runs no code.
touches: Nothing: it makes no network requests, reads no conversations or memory, and runs no browser or server code.
may_change: Loam's colour palette in light and dark modes, display heading font (Young Serif), and appearance options for agent avatar shapes and marks when selected as your active theme.
worth_knowing: The Young Serif display font is bundled locally as WOFF2 files, so no external font service is contacted.

plugins.name: Deep Forest
plugins.description: Mossy greens and soft canopy light, for a calmer Loam by day and by night.
plugins.author: Michael Hejazi

note.summary: Deep Forest is a visual theme that dresses Loam in mossy greens and soft canopy colours for both light and dark modes, pairing them with the Fraunces display font for headings. It contains only CSS stylesheets, local font files, and preview images, and runs no code.
touches: Nothing outside appearance: it makes no network requests, reads no conversations or memory, and runs no code in your browser or on your server.
may_change: Loam's colour palette in light and dark modes through CSS custom properties.
The display font used for headings (to a bundled copy of Fraunces).
Appearance options for agent avatar shapes and whether avatars show a mark or initials.
worth_knowing: The Fraunces font files are bundled directly in the plugin, so your browser does not contact an external font service to load them.

plugins.name: Dictation
plugins.description: Talk instead of typing: say it, and tidy words land in your draft.
plugins.author: Michael Hejazi

note.summary: Dictation adds a microphone button to the composer, full-screen editor, and file editor so you can speak into your draft instead of typing. It records your take and sends it through its own plugin server to Google Gemini or OpenAI for transcription and optional cleanup, or falls back to your browser's built-in live speech recognition when no server key is set.
touches: Your microphone in the browser while you are recording a take

generativelanguage.googleapis.com from the plugin's server when a Google Gemini key is configured, sending recorded audio, custom vocabulary terms, and the resulting transcript (when Polish is Light or Full)

api.openai.com from the plugin's server when an OpenAI key is configured and no Google key is present, sending recorded audio, custom vocabulary terms, and the resulting transcript (when Polish is Light or Full)
Your browser's built-in speech recognition service when you choose 'As you speak' mode or when no server API key is configured

Your current conversation (the agent's name, thread title, and capitalized names from the last 8 messages) and the file 'Dictation terms.md' in your vault's system folder, read to bias spelling toward names and terms you use
Runs a local Node server on your Loam host that holds the Google Gemini and OpenAI API keys and reads your dictation terms note
may_change: Adds a microphone button and an inline recording bar to the composer, full-screen editor, and file editor, and inserts transcribed words at your cursor
Adds a Dictation preferences section in Settings and saves your mode, polish level, maximum recording length, and chosen microphone in this browser's device settings
Adds an optional key setup dialog that can verify and save a Google Gemini API key to your Loam Connections settings when you paste one in
worth_knowing: It only inserts words into your draft at the cursor; it never sends a message or saves a file on its own.
It checks for a Google Gemini key first, then an OpenAI key, and falls back to browser speech recognition if neither key is provided.

In 'Record first' mode, capitalized words from the last 8 messages of the open conversation and terms from your 'Dictation terms.md' note are sent to the active speech provider alongside the audio to help it spell names right.

When Polish is set to Light or Full, a second request is sent to Gemini or OpenAI with `store: false`, and a local check falls back to the unpolished transcript if the model adds unfamiliar proper nouns, changes the word count too much, or replies as a chatbot.
changed: Reaches api.openai.com and requests your optional OpenAI API key to transcribe and polish recordings when no Google Gemini key is configured.
Makes the Google Gemini key optional so the plugin can run with an OpenAI key or browser-only speech recognition.
Adds an in-app guide dialog (`app.overlay`) to verify and save a Google Gemini API key into Loam's Connections settings.

plugins.name: Foundry
plugins.description: Steel, concrete and patina: a crisp, workmanlike Loam with square corners and a bold display face.
plugins.author: Michael Hejazi

note.summary: Foundry is a visual theme for Loam that styles light and dark modes with steel, plaster, and cast-iron colours, sharper corners, and the Big Shoulders Display heading font. It contains only CSS, local font files, and preview images, and runs no code.
touches: Nothing: it makes no network requests, reads no conversations or memory, and runs no code in your browser or on your server.
may_change: Loam's appearance when chosen in Settings › Appearance: colour palette in light and dark modes, corner rounding, heading font (Big Shoulders Display), and agent face shape options.
worth_knowing: The Big Shoulders Display font files are bundled inside the plugin (`display-latin.woff2` and `display-latin-ext.woff2`), so loading the font does not contact any external font host.

plugins.name: Mist Trail
plugins.description: Waterfall spray, fir shade and cedar bark: a cool, fresh Loam that feels like a morning walk.
plugins.author: Michael Hejazi

note.summary: Mist Trail is a visual theme for Loam inspired by forest shade, morning fog, and cedar bark, with palettes for both light and dark modes. It includes only CSS token definitions, bundled font files, and preview images, and runs no code.
touches: Nothing: it makes no network requests, reads no conversations or memory, and runs no code in the browser or on the server.
may_change: Loam's colour palette in light and dark modes.
The display heading font (sets it to the bundled DM Serif Display).
Appearance options for agent face shapes and inner marks or initials when selected.
worth_knowing: The DM Serif Display font files are bundled locally in the plugin folder, so loading the font does not contact any external font service.

plugins.name: Read aloud
plugins.description: Listen to your agents instead of reading them, each in a voice of its own.
plugins.author: Michael Hejazi

note.summary: Read aloud adds a speaker button to agent replies and markdown notes in Files so you can listen to them or hear a shorter spoken summary. It runs a local plugin server on your Loam that generates and caches speech using Google Gemini or OpenAI when a key is configured, or falls back to your browser's built-in speech synthesis without a key.
touches: generativelanguage.googleapis.com — sends the text of a reply or markdown note (and table or diagram blocks when descriptions are enabled) from your server when you ask to prepare or play audio, using your Google Gemini API key

api.openai.com — sends the text of a reply or markdown note (and table or diagram blocks when descriptions are enabled) over HTTPS and WebSockets from your server when an OpenAI API key is configured and no Google key is present

Browser speech services (browser-managed) — passes reply or note text to your browser's SpeechSynthesis engine when neither a Google nor an OpenAI key is configured, which may use a remote speech service managed by your browser or operating system
Your conversations (read) — reads agent reply text, thread titles, and agent names to prepare speech and summaries
Your Files notes (read) — reads the markdown note currently open in Files when you ask to read it aloud

Your server — runs a Node server process that calls Google Gemini or OpenAI, runs ffmpeg to encode MP3 audio, and caches generated audio and table/diagram descriptions in the plugin's private folder for up to 48 hours
may_change: Adds a speaker button and player under agent replies, a Read aloud action and duration sheet in Files, and a docked player bar across screens while audio is active
Adds a voice picker with bundled audio samples to each agent's profile, reading preferences in Settings, and a guided sheet that can verify and save a Google Gemini API key to your Loam Connections

Saves your reading preferences (word thresholds, playback rate, Files voice, and whether tables and diagrams are described) in browser storage on each device, and each agent's voice in its profile or plugin settings
worth_knowing: Uses a Google Gemini key first, then an OpenAI key, and falls back to your browser's built-in voice if no key is set; spoken summaries (Brief), table/diagram descriptions, and seeking are only available with a server key and ffmpeg (with libmp3lame) installed on the server.
Your Google Gemini and OpenAI API keys stay on the server and are never sent to the browser, and text is only sent to the active provider when you request audio or a sample.
Generated MP3 files and cached table or diagram descriptions are kept on disk in the plugin's private directory and automatically swept after 48 hours of inactivity.
changed: No new hosts, permissions, or data access compared to version 1.2.0.
Updates the Gemini key setup guide to use Loam's shared menu surface and only shows the setup link in Settings when using the browser voice fallback.

plugins.name: Syncthing
plugins.description: Your notes on your own phone and laptop, kept in sync with no cloud in between.
plugins.author: Michael Hejazi

note.summary: Lets your agents check Syncthing on your server and pair your phone or laptop to sync your Loam vault directly between your devices. The plugin talks only to Syncthing's local control address on 127.0.0.1 using the API key Loam imports from your local Syncthing configuration.
touches: 127.0.0.1 (Syncthing's local REST API on this machine, to check status and configure devices and folders)
Your Syncthing API key, imported by Loam from ~/.local/state/syncthing/config.xml or ~/.config/syncthing/config.xml and handed to the plugin
Your entire vault, including conversations and shared agent memory, which Syncthing syncs both ways with the devices you pair
may_change: Adds devices you ask to pair to your local Syncthing configuration
Registers your Loam vault folder in Syncthing (with .git excluded in .stignore) and shares it with paired devices
Any files in your vault, including conversations and memory, when paired devices sync changes back to this machine
worth_knowing: Syncthing must already be installed and running as your user on the server, with its GUI bound to 127.0.0.1 or localhost.
Unpairing a device through the agent stops sharing the vault folder with that device, though the device entry itself stays in Syncthing's known devices list.
changed: Declares a Syncthing key under keys so Loam imports the API key and local GUI URL from Syncthing's config.xml at install time and supplies them via LOAM_PLUGIN_KEYS, instead of the plugin reading config.xml directly.
Connects directly to 127.0.0.1 via http.client without following HTTP redirects or environment proxies, and rejects non-loopback control addresses.

plugins.name: Yosemite
plugins.description: Granite walls, meadow grasses and big sky, with the friendly lettering of a park sign.
plugins.author: Michael Hejazi

note.summary: Yosemite is a light and dark colour theme inspired by granite walls, meadow grasses and national park signage, with headings set in Zilla Slab. It contains only CSS, local font files and preview images, and runs no code.
touches: Nothing outside how Loam looks: no network hosts, conversations, memory or server code.
may_change: Loam's light and dark colour palette, display heading font (Zilla Slab), and the shape and content of agent faces when chosen in Settings › Appearance.
worth_knowing: The Zilla Slab font files are bundled inside the plugin and loaded locally rather than fetched from an external font host.
Includes appearance options for agent face shapes (Signature, Each its own, Circle, Rounded square) and face content (Mark, Initials).
changed: Nothing widened in what the plugin reaches; this update adds a changelog to the README and updates the install link to v1.0.4.
